title: M3b: Phase-6-min offline subsystem (Rust)
description:
M3b — second phase of M3, gated on M3a completion.

Scope: minimum Rust offline subsystem required to pass
PILOT_ACCEPTANCE_TEST_PLAN Phase 6 (offline lifecycle: enter offline,
issue receipts under OFFLINE_LOCAL_ACK, block Z-report on backlog,
return online, sync, finalize).

This is NOT full WebCheck parity. 36h/168h offline-limit enforcement
and the 24h shift guard are NOT part of Phase-6-min unless promoted
into M3b; omitting them from a live pilot requires explicit owner
risk acceptance before Go.

In scope (per handoff §3.1):
  - Offline session lifecycle: open / drain / close OFFLINE_LOCAL_ACK pool
  - OFFLINE_LOCAL_ACK whitelist extension to 6 targets + retry self-loop
  - ix_offline_active UNIQUE migration
  - Pattern C "stage and flip" envelope-then-finalize
  - Auto-flip OFFLINE -> ONLINE via ping(fn_sign)
  - Offline-code availability and offline-code-pool bounds (without
    these Phase 6 has no meaning)

Out of scope for M3b (canonically owned elsewhere):
  - Generic SENDING-state reconciler (last_chk cooldown for operator-
    stuck docs) — owned by M5, NOT M3b
  - Operator manual-reconciliation hooks — owned by M5/M6 (CLI per ADR D2)
  - Web admin UI — out of pilot scope per ADR D2
  - Backup/restore, key/CA rotation, rollback rehearsal — parallel
    docs+ops track per ADR D3, NOT part of M3b
  - 36h/168h offline limits, 24h shift guard — owner risk acceptance,
    not promoted into M3b unless explicitly decided

Anchored on:
  - ADR docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-07-pilot-runtime-decision.md
    (Status: ACCEPTED, commit 45aa6f9)
  - docs/M3-W0-handoff.md §3.1 (commit 1cc5ce5)

Blocked by M3a completion (PRRO_GATE-9qd.1).
acceptance_criteria:
PILOT_ACCEPTANCE_TEST_PLAN Phase 6 passes against Rust-only stack:
offline session lifecycle (open/drain/close OFFLINE_LOCAL_ACK pool),
OFFLINE_LOCAL_ACK whitelist transitions, Z-report guard while backlog
non-empty, sync-back to final ACK after return-online.

Generic SENDING-state reconciler is NOT required by this acceptance
(owned by M5, not M3b).

Omission of 36h/168h offline-limit enforcement and 24h shift guard
from this milestone requires explicit owner risk acceptance recorded

title: M-series: Rust-only pilot path (M3a-M6)
description:
Scope envelope: Rust-only pilot path — five-milestone sequence
M3a → M3b → M4 → M5 → M6.

Per ADR docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-07-pilot-runtime-decision.md
(Status: ACCEPTED, commit 45aa6f9), the path from a working Rust
write-path to a live pilot is a Rust-only sequence in which Python is
removed from the pilot runtime entirely.  This epic is the umbrella;
each phase is a child epic with its own scope and acceptance:

  - 9qd.1 M3a — ONLINE happy-path 5-stage write-path
    (acquire+validate -> guard -> sign -> send -> finalize).  ONLINE
    node only; no offline writes, no operator recovery flows, no
    full reconciliation.
  - 9qd.2 M3b — Phase-6-min offline subsystem (minimum Rust offline
    lifecycle to pass PILOT_ACCEPTANCE_TEST_PLAN Phase 6).  NOT full
    WebCheck parity.  Generic SENDING reconciler is M5, not M3b.
    Operator manual-reconciliation flows are M5/M6, not M3b.
  - 9qd.3 M4 — Rust ingress + transport bridges (REST, XML-RPC,
    Maria-shell, maria304_driver re-bridge to in-process gateway,
    optional 1С OLE per ADR open item O1 closure).
  - 9qd.4 M5 — services tail (ingress writer, generic SENDING
    reconciler, post-boot reconciliation hooks, manual-reconcile
    CLI surface, optional cert_provisioning / retention /
    shift_aggregation per ADR open items O2 / O3).  Backup/restore
    is NOT in M5; see handoff §3.5 parallel docs+ops track.
  - 9qd.5 M6 — admin surface; prro_admin CLI only for pilot.  Web
    admin UI is post-pilot.

All phases bind to M2 substrate (prro::crypto, prro::transports::dps,
prro::xml, services::cert_refresher; see docs/M2-handoff.md §2 for
frozen contracts).

Inputs (frozen):
  - docs/M2-handoff.md (§4 names the 10 inviolable invariants and
    5 M3-entry decisions).
  - docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-06-m3-w0-research.md
    (M3-W0 research mini-plan).
  - docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-04-m2-pre-plan-adr.md
    (M2 ADRs M2-1..M2-6 approved 2026-05-04; M3 ADR amendments
    A1..A9 added in commit 8c72a14).
  - docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-07-pilot-runtime-decision.md
    (Pilot Runtime ADR, Status: ACCEPTED, commit 45aa6f9).
  - docs/M3-W0-handoff.md §3.1-§3.5 (post-M3a deferrals updated
    per pilot runtime ADR, commit 1cc5ce5).
  - docs/Multi-Protocol_PRRO_Gateway.md (technical spec).

Decomposition order: M3a -> M3b -> M4 -> M5 -> M6, enforced by bd
dep chain (9qd.1 -> 9qd.2 -> 9qd.3 -> 9qd.4 -> 9qd.5).  Each phase
opens ready in bd only after its predecessor closes.

Cross-links (set at epic creation):
  parent-child to phase children:
    - PRRO_GATE-9qd.1 (M3a)
    - PRRO_GATE-9qd.2 (M3b)
    - PRRO_GATE-9qd.3 (M4)
    - PRRO_GATE-9qd.4 (M5)
    - PRRO_GATE-9qd.5 (M6)
  parent-child to M3a-supporting bd issues (carried at the M3a
  level via 9qd.1, listed here for tree visibility):
    - PRRO_GATE-ddn (lnd monotonicity) — M3a W1 + W5

title: M3 write_path: WebCheck-derived submit retry/recovery policy
description:
WebCheck SubmitPtr.cs:50 implements a non-trivial policy on top of
the typed-error mapping our M2 transport ships:

  - status -3 (ERROR_SAVE on the wire today; WebCheck's marker for
    "transient persist failure server-side") → retry with backoff.
  - status -15 (ERROR_NOT_OPEN_SHIFT) → recovery via lastChk; the
    write-path consults lastChk to reconcile the FN's current
    server state before the next submit.
  - status 0 (UNKNOWN / missing field) → treated as decode + retry
    with reconciliation, NOT as a hard failure.
  - status -16 (ERROR_OFFLINE_ID) → offline-technical path: the
    document was rejected because of an offline-id mismatch, which
    triggers WebCheck's offline-pool reconciliation rather than a
    plain retry.

Our M2 W3 transport currently TYPES these errors (Server { code,
message } / Decode / Authorization / Transport per W0-1 review) but
does NOT implement the routing policy.  The routing belongs in
M3's services::write_path, NOT in the transport — but it MUST land
before pilot.

Without this policy, M3 write_path will treat every non-OK status
as "fail the document and stop", which would be brittle in
production where transient -3 / -15 / -16 outcomes are expected
parts of the lifecycle.

Acceptance (M3-targeted):
  - status -3 retry/backoff policy implemented in services::write_path
    with bounded attempts + exponential backoff + audit_log entry per
    retry.
  - status -15 / status 0 lastChk reconciliation path: on these
    statuses, write_path calls last_chk to learn the FN's current
    server-side state, then decides retry vs hard-fail vs offline.
  - status -16 offline-id / technical offline path decision: either
    (a) implement offline-pool reconciliation in M3, or (b)
    explicitly defer offline lifecycle to a separate milestone (see
    PRRO_GATE-er6 + the offline-lifecycle parity follow-up).
  - All policy state changes happen OUTSIDE network/crypto calls
    (invariant #1: no network/crypto inside a tx).
  - Targeted tests cover each branch (retry, reconciliation,
    offline-technical) using a mock DpsChannel.

Evidence: docs/webcheck_reverse/WebCheckMain/WebCheck/SubmitPtr.cs:50
acceptance_criteria: M3 services::write_path implements: status -3 bounded retry+backoff with audit; status -15/0 lastChk reconciliation; status -16 offline-id decision (implement OR explicit defer); no network/crypto inside any tx; targeted tests cover each branch with a mock DpsChannel.

title: DPS TLS CA bundle support for GrpcDpsChannel
description:
WebCheck loads a CA bundle PEM file and constructs an SSL credential
explicitly:

  TaxGrpc/Client.cs:34 — reads
  C:\ProgramData\WebCheck\prro-tax-gov-ua-chain.pem
  and creates a tonic-equivalent `SslCredentials(rootCerts: pem)`.

Our M2 W3 `GrpcDpsChannel::connect(endpoint, request_timeout)`
currently passes the URI through `tonic::transport::Endpoint`, which
relies on the system TLS root store.  Production DPS endpoints may
require:

  - explicit CA-bundle pinning (the chain WebCheck ships, or its
    successor) so the gateway works on hosts without the relevant
    Ukrainian CA roots in /etc/ssl/certs;
  - test-vs-prod CA isolation (separate bundles per environment so a
    test-CA can never accidentally validate a prod cert);
  - SNI / hostname-verify rules for the cabinet.tax.gov.ua endpoint.

Without this, the gateway can fail TLS handshake at first prod call —
exactly the kind of failure that would manifest only in pilot.

Acceptance:
  - GrpcDpsChannel exposes a typed config for an optional CA bundle
    path (PEM file).
  - test-vs-prod separation preserved; mock/test path still works
    without a CA bundle (wiremock / tonic mock are plain HTTP/2).
  - Documented in W3 plan + a small ops note (CA bundle location +
    rotation procedure).
  - Pilot smoke test verifies a real prod TLS handshake succeeds.

Evidence: docs/webcheck_reverse/TaxGrpc/TaxGrpc/Client.cs:34
acceptance_criteria: GrpcDpsChannel takes optional CA-bundle PEM path; test/prod CA isolation preserved; mock path still works; ops doc covers rotation; pilot smoke test verifies real-prod TLS handshake.

title: DPS proto drift vs WebCheck TaxGrpc decompilation
description:
WebCheck TaxGrpc generated service surface (decompilation) carries
EIGHT unary RPCs; our M2 W3 proto + DpsChannel implements only FIVE:

  Implemented (M2 W3 in scope):
    - sendChkV2
    - lastChk
    - ping
    - statusRro
    - infoRro

  Generated by WebCheck but NOT in our proto (drift):
    - sendChk        (legacy API v1 submit; WebCheck routes API v1 → sendChk
                      and API v2 → sendChkV2 in TaxGrpc/Client.cs:57,114.
                      Default verAPIdefault = 2 in WebCheck/All.cs:20, so
                      new pilots can default to v2.)
    - delLastChk     (last-receipt destructive cancel; not exposed in the
                      public WebCheck IClient.cs:7 surface, only generated.
                      Recovery / admin op; MUST NOT fold into the normal
                      DpsChannel without a separate ADR + audit gate.)
    - delLastChkId   (id-targeted destructive cancel using
                      CheckRequestId { id, rro_fn_sign }; same recovery /
                      admin classification.)

Decision points to surface BEFORE M2 → pilot scope review:

  1. sendChk v1 — defer or implement?
     Recommendation: defer.  Rationale: WebCheck default is v2; new
     pilots can be configured for v2 from day one.  Migration path
     for legacy WebCheck configs that hard-code apiver=1 needs an
     explicit "auto-migrate or refuse" decision.

  2. delLastChk / delLastChkId — defer or implement?
     Recommendation: defer to a separate "DpsAdminOps / manual
     recovery" ADR.  Rationale: these are destructive/admin
     operations.  Mixing them into DpsChannel risks accidental
     cancellation; they need:
       - typed admin-only API surface (e.g. DpsAdminChannel trait)
       - audit_log entry on every call
       - hard gate (CLI flag / admin role / ops-only feature flag)
       - reconciliation rules with services::write_path

  3. CheckRequestId proto message — same defer (only delLastChkId
     consumes it).

  4. WebCheck COM/1C public TaxGrpc IClient exposes only Open /
     Check / Ping / CheckLast (IClient.cs:7), so the delLast* surface
     is generated-but-private even in WebCheck.  Pilot-level scope
     therefore looks like:
       - 5 RPC are mandatory for production parity.
       - sendChk v1 is mandatory IF a pilot config requires apiver=1.
       - delLast* are admin/recovery and stay deferred unless an
         operator workflow explicitly requires them.

W3 sign-off gate for M2: this issue MUST be resolved (with documented
decisions) before M2 → pilot scope review.

Acceptance:
  - Decision recorded in ADR + W3 plan.
  - sendChk v1 either implemented OR explicitly deferred with
    migration plan for apiver=1 configs.
  - delLastChk / delLastChkId either implemented behind a separate
    DpsAdminChannel trait + audit gate OR explicitly deferred to a
    follow-up ADR.
  - W3 sign-off references this decision.

Evidence:
  - docs/webcheck_reverse/TaxGrpc/Com.Programika.Rro.Ws.Chk/ChkIncomeService.cs:15,257
  - docs/webcheck_reverse/TaxGrpc/Com.Programika.Rro.Ws.Chk/CheckRequestId.cs:14
  - docs/webcheck_reverse/TaxGrpc/TaxGrpc/IClient.cs:7
  - docs/webcheck_reverse/TaxGrpc/TaxGrpc/Client.cs:57,114
  - docs/webcheck_reverse/WebCheckMain/WebCheck/All.cs:20
  - rust/prro/proto/fiscal_server.proto:8

Discovered during W3-C3 review (commit 42f02ba); body refreshed during
docs-only pilot-parity review (2026-05-05).
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded in ADR + W3 plan; sendChk v1 either implemented OR explicitly deferred with apiver=1 migration plan; delLastChk/delLastChkId either implemented behind a separate DpsAdminChannel trait + audit gate OR explicitly deferred to a follow-up ADR; W3 sign-off references this decision.

title: M2 W1+: ByServerFiscalNo gRPC channel = lastChk(fn_sign) + response.id match, not direct server-id lookup
description: W0-1 review note: lastChk RPC is not a true wire-level 'lookup by server_fiscal_no' — the request carries the signed FN, and the client compares response.id against the expected fiscal id.  Acceptable under single-writer / recovery preconditions (M1 invariant #2), but the M2 W1+ DpsChannel implementation and tonic mock must encode this explicitly: the ByServerFiscalNo path is lastChk(fn_sign) + response.id match, not a direct server-id query.  Tests must cover: (a) match path -> Ok(record), (b) mismatch path -> typed error (server returned a different fiscal id than expected), (c) absent path -> NotFound.  Source: M2-W0-1 findings doc docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-04-m2-w0-1-dps-wire.md sections covering lastChk semantics, plus the user review note on 2026-05-04.
acceptance_criteria: DpsChannel impl in M2 W1+ documents the semantic; tonic mock supports the match/mismatch/absent triple; integration test covers all three branches; findings doc cited from the M2 W1+ implementation plan.

title: Pilot decision: print/export/check URL parity
description:
WebCheck PrintExportCheck.cs:121 builds receipt URLs (cabinet
verification links), drives print/export, and exposes the operator-
facing rendering surface.  Our M2/M3 has none of this — rendering
lives in the M5 milestone per the project's CLAUDE.md architecture
note.

This is a pilot-readiness checkpoint:

  - Pilot operators expect printed receipts with the official
    `https://cabinet.tax.gov.ua/cabinet/faces/login.xhtml#... ` URL
    (or current equivalent) so the customer can verify the receipt.
  - Operators may also need PDF / HTML export of the day's receipt
    set for accounting reconciliation.
  - WebCheck integrates this into its own print pipeline; we'll
    need to either match its URL/format conventions or document
    the divergence to operators.

Acceptance:
  - Pilot survey: which print/export formats does each pilot
    operator need?  (ESC-POS thermal, A4 PDF, HTML, none?)
  - Decision recorded: priority for M5 print/export work.
  - If "blocker for pilot": bumps priority to P1 + lands in M5
    (or a pilot-only print shim earlier).
  - If "deferred": pilot operators sign off on no-print or use
    their existing WebCheck-style printer.

Evidence: docs/webcheck_reverse/WebCheckMain/WebCheck/PrintExportCheck.cs:121
acceptance_criteria: Pilot survey identifies print/export needs per operator; decision recorded; priority bumps to P1 if blocker; M5 print/export milestone scope adjusted accordingly.

title: Pilot decision: WebCheck COM/1C 19-method compatibility
description:
WebCheckServer exposes a 19-method COM/OLE surface to 1C and other
Windows clients (vk_WebCheckServer.cs:20-, GetNMethods = 19 at
vk_WebCheckServer.cs:245).  If a pilot client is still running on
WebCheck's COM/1C integration, our Rust gateway needs either:

  (a) a compatibility shim — a Windows-side process that exposes the
      same 19-method COM surface and proxies to the gateway over
      gRPC / HTTP / IPC, OR
  (b) a print-only / out-of-band integration where 1C drives the
      gateway via a different protocol (REST, signed-doc file
      drop, etc.) and bypasses COM entirely.

Today neither is in M2 scope.  This is a pilot decision, not an
M2/M3 implementation task.

Acceptance:
  - Pilot survey: which pilot operators rely on WebCheck COM/1C?
    (priority bumps to P1 if any do; stays P2 if all pilots can
    skip COM.)
  - Decision recorded: shim vs out-of-band.
  - If shim: separate ADR + scope estimate before commit.
  - If out-of-band: 1C integration path documented for pilot
    operators.

Evidence:
  - docs/webcheck_reverse/WebCheckServer/WebCheckServer/vk_WebCheckServer.cs:20
  - docs/webcheck_reverse/WebCheckServer/WebCheckServer/vk_WebCheckServer.cs:245
acceptance_criteria: Pilot survey identifies whether any operator depends on WebCheck COM/1C; decision recorded (shim vs out-of-band); if shim, separate ADR + scope estimate; priority bumps to P1 if any pilot needs it.

title: Concurrent race test for IngressInboxRepo idempotency
description: Existing tests in rust/prro/tests/repo_ingress_inbox_idempotency.rs prove sequential branches (Created/Replay/Conflict).  Code + with_immediate + UNIQUE(fn, idem_key) make the concurrent claim 'loser sees winner and returns Replay/Conflict' true by construction, but no test exercises the race directly.  Add a tokio multi-thread test that fires N concurrent insert() calls with the same (fn, idem_key) and asserts exactly one Created and N-1 Replays (or Conflicts if hashes differ).
acceptance_criteria: tokio multi_thread test fires >=8 concurrent inserts with same (fn, idem_key); exactly one returns Created, the rest Replay; SELECT COUNT(*) = 1 in ingress_inbox

title: Type-safe wrappers in IngressInboxRepo (RequestId, InboxStatus)

Behaviour is correct, but the public API exposes loose primitives.  Convert before any external call site lands (M3 ingress shell).
acceptance_criteria: InboxRow.request_id: RequestId, InboxRow.status: InboxStatus, NewInboxEntry.request_id: RequestId; tests updated to typed values; no functional change

title: W6 follow-up: feature-gate pub mod test_hook + production call site
description: Senior Rust review §9 LOW + 3rd-party reviewer LOW/optional: rust/prro/src/services/write_path/stage_sign.rs:139 declares 'pub mod test_hook' unconditionally; rust/prro/src/services/write_path/stage_sign.rs:372 calls 'test_hook::record_persist_first()' on the production hot path. Drifts from frozen W6 spec language 'debug/test-only hook' but is not a functional bug — atomic fetch_add overhead per signed doc is negligible. Cleaner fix: add Cargo feature 'test-hooks', wrap module + call site behind #[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-hooks"))]; keep no-op stub when feature absent. Update CI to enable feature for 'cargo test' invocations. Not blocking PR #25.

title: W6 follow-up: convert document_files runtime queries to query!/query_scalar! macros

title: Workspace hardening: move non-root Cargo profiles to workspace root or remove them
description: cargo build/test -p prro emits warnings: profiles for non root package will be ignored for rust/prro_crypto/Cargo.toml and rust/prro_sidecar/Cargo.toml. M1 self-review says cargo build should be clean with zero warnings; current build passes but is not warning-clean. Decide whether those profiles should be moved to rust/Cargo.toml [profile.*] / [profile.*.package.*] or removed from member crates.
acceptance_criteria: cargo build -p prro --locked and cargo test -p prro --locked no longer print Cargo warnings about ignored profiles; intended release/profile settings are preserved at workspace root if still needed.
